@graph.rdfs:label: temporalCoverage
@graph.name: temporalCoverage
@graph.rdfs:comment:
The temporalCoverage of a CreativeWork indicates the period that the content applies to, i.e. that it describes, either as a DateTime or as a textual string indicating a time period in [ISO 8601 time interval format](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_8601#Time_intervals). In
      the case of a Dataset it will typically indicate the relevant time period in a precise notation (e.g. for a 2011 census dataset, the year 2011 would be written "2011/2012"). Other forms of content, e.g. ScholarlyArticle, Book, TVSeries or TVEpisode, may indicate their temporalCoverage in broader terms - textually or via well-known URL.
      Written works such as books may sometimes have precise temporal coverage too, e.g. a work set in 1939 - 1945 can be indicated in ISO 8601 interval format format via "1939/1945".

Open-ended date ranges can be written with ".." in place of the end date. For example, "2015-11/.." indicates a range beginning in November 2015 and with no specified final date. This is tentative and might be updated in future when ISO 8601 is officially updated.

@graph.rdfs:label: identifier

@graph.rdfs:comment: The identifier property represents any kind of identifier for any kind of [[Thing]], such as ISBNs, GTIN codes, UUIDs etc. Schema.org provides dedicated properties for representing many of these, either as textual strings or as URL (URI) links. See [background notes](/docs/datamodel.html#identifierBg) for more details.

The resource includes material that adds information to some other linguistic record.
@graph.name: Annotation

@graph.description: This is derived from another source, such as a Primary Material, via some process, e.g. a downsampled video or a sample or an abstract of a resource that is not an annotation (an analysis or description).

@graph.name: ldac:materialType

AccessTypes
@graph.description: Set of defined terms for ldac:access
Data covered by this license may be accessed as long as the license is served alongside it, and does not require any specific authorization step.
@graph.name: OpenAccess

@graph.rdfs:label: ldac:access
@graph.name: ldac:access
@graph.rdfs:comment: Whether this is an open or restricted access license.

@graph.rdfs:label: ldac:accessControlList
@graph.name: ldac:accessControlList
@graph.rdfs:comment: When a license has an authorizationWorkflow property with a value of the DefinedTerm AccessControlList this property has a URI value that points to a list of userIDs.

@graph.description: License grants access to data based on a list of approved users, specified using the property accessControlList.
@graph.name: AccessControlList
AuthorizationWorkflows
@graph.description: Set of defined terms for ldac:authorizationWorkflow

A user is expected to explicitly agree to a set of license terms, this may be combined with AccessControlList - to note that even if a user has been pre-approved for a license they must agree to license terms.
@graph.name: AgreeToTerms

@graph.description: Users may apply for a license via some workflow, such as a form, with the decision being made by a DataSteward or their delegate about whether to grant the license.
@graph.name: AuthorizationByApplication

@graph.description: A data steward or administrator is expected to use an access control system to invite users, for example, participants, collaborators or students.
@graph.name: AuthorizationByInvitation

@graph.description: A user can be authorised to access data by clicking that they agree to a license, or filling out a form to check their understanding, which can be validated by a machine and does not require human intervention.
@graph.name: SelfAuthorization

@graph.rdfs:label: ldac:authorizationWorkflow
@graph.name: ldac:authorizationWorkflow
@graph.rdfs:comment: By what process a user is granted authorization to a license.
